items.title: Mcbee interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2020
items.q: my first recording we discussed before, with Grachan Moncur featuring Herbie Hancock, Wayne Shorter and Tony Williams.

ctx.x: Beautiful. Just to wrap up, an acquaintance knew I was going to be talking to you and he said, “Oh he’s played with everyone. I’m curious if he ever recorded with Miles Davis?”

No. I didn’t record with Miles Davis, but I had an episode with Miles Davis. Herbie Hancock called me — well what’s that, my first recording we discussed before, with Grachan Moncur featuring Herbie Hancock, Wayne Shorter and Tony Williams. This is how I met Herbie and those guys. And so apparently I was rather impressive with my dynamic. Herbie called me and says, “Miles would like you to do a performance with him.” So I said, “Yeah, okay.” And by now, I mean that was like a couple of years later. By now I’m…

mean playing with Jack and Keith were just all I was about. But on 77th Street on the third floor of Miles’ brownstone we had gone through all the tunes, the music was like that — right? And no Miles Davis. Right? So at the conclusion of the rehearsal, the last tune in the Key of C there was Herbie and Wayne were at the piano discussing the voicing of a G something chord, a G 7 chord. And they couldn’t find it. All of a sudden burst through the door was Miles Davis. He went over to the piano and he said…
